mc-moose-002.back: Only bulls (90%). Both sexes have a bell, so the bell does not prove a bull.

mc-moose-003.front: Cow moose in the synopsis definition?
mc-moose-003.back: No antlers, 1.8 m at the shoulder, 340 to 420 kg (99%, page 3).

mc-moose-004.front: Calf moose in the synopsis definition?
mc-moose-004.back: Under 12 months, usually under 1.5 m at the shoulder, 135 to 180 kg (99%, page 3).

mc-moose-005.back: Nearly 2 m at the shoulder; 450 to 500 kg in autumn; record 595 kg (90%).

mc-moose-016.front: Why did central BC moose decline in the early 2000s?
mc-moose-016.back: Pine beetle salvage logging and roads made moose easier for hunters and predators (90%, BC hypothesis).

mc-moose-017.front: Are moose common in the dry Thompson valley?
mc-moose-017.back: No. Scarce in dry southern valleys like the Thompson and Okanagan (90%).
